faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Quick answers to the most common questions from expats living in Saudi Arabia.

items.question: What is an Iqama and why do I need it?
items.answer: An Iqama (إقامة) is a residency permit issued to all expatriates living and working in Saudi Arabia. It is your legal identification document in the Kingdom and is required for virtually all official transactions — opening a bank account, renting an apartment, getting a SIM card, accessing healthcare, and renewing your driving license. Your employer (sponsor) is legally responsible for obtaining and renewing your Iqama.

items.question: How do I renew my Iqama before it expires?
items.answer: Your sponsor or HR department is primarily responsible for Iqama renewal. However, you can monitor your Iqama status and expiry date through the Absher platform (absher.sa) or the Muqeem portal. Renewal typically requires paying a government fee (currently SAR 650/year for most nationalities), ensuring your health insurance is active, and that your employer's Nitaqat compliance status is in good standing. Start the process at least 30 days before expiry to avoid fines.

items.question: Can I change jobs in Saudi Arabia without losing my residency?
items.answer: Yes, under the Labor Reform Initiative (LRI) introduced in 2021, most expatriates can transfer their sponsorship (Iqama) to a new employer without requiring the current employer's consent, provided they have completed at least one year of service. You can initiate a job transfer through the Absher platform. There are certain restrictions for domestic workers and some sectors — check the official HRSD portal for the latest eligibility criteria.

items.question: What is an Exit Re-Entry Visa and do I need one?
items.answer: An Exit Re-Entry Visa (تأشيرة الخروج والعودة) is required if you want to leave Saudi Arabia and return. Without it, leaving the country may be treated as a Final Exit, cancelling your Iqama. You can apply for single or multiple exit re-entry visas through Absher. As of 2021, most expatriates no longer need employer permission to obtain an exit re-entry visa after completing one year of service, thanks to the Labor Reform Initiative.

items.question: How is End of Service Benefit (EOSB) calculated?
items.answer: Under Saudi Labor Law, EOSB (gratuity) is calculated based on your last basic salary and years of service. For the first 5 years: half a month's salary per year. After 5 years: one full month's salary per year. If you resign before completing 2 years, you receive no EOSB. Between 2-5 years, you receive one-third of the entitlement. Between 5-10 years, you receive two-thirds. After 10 years, you receive the full amount.

items.question: What health insurance is required for expats in Saudi Arabia?
items.answer: Saudi Arabia mandates that all employers provide health insurance for their expatriate employees and their sponsored dependents under the Cooperative Health Insurance System regulated by the Council of Cooperative Health Insurance (CCHI). The minimum coverage (Class C) covers basic inpatient and outpatient treatment. Employers who fail to provide health insurance face significant fines and Nitaqat compliance penalties.

items.question: How do I get a Saudi driving license as an expatriate?
items.answer: The process depends on your nationality and the type of license you hold. Citizens of GCC countries and nationals of certain countries with reciprocal agreements (including the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and many European nations) can exchange their foreign license directly at the traffic department (Muroor) without taking a test. Other nationalities must complete a driving course at a licensed driving school and pass both a theory and practical exam.

items.question: Is it safe to live in Saudi Arabia as an expat?
items.answer: Saudi Arabia consistently ranks as one of the safest countries in the world for expatriates. Violent crime rates are very low. The main considerations for expats are traffic safety (road accidents are a leading cause of injury), workplace rights awareness, and understanding local laws and cultural norms. Alcohol is strictly prohibited, and public behavior is governed by local customs. Most expats report feeling very safe in their daily lives across all major Saudi cities.

aboutPage.heroDescription: URExpat is an independent information platform dedicated to helping expatriates navigate life in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia with confidence, clarity, and accuracy.

mission.label: Our Mission
mission.title: Why We Exist
mission.p1: Saudi Arabia is home to over 13 million expatriates — nearly 40% of the total population. Yet for most of them, navigating the Kingdom's bureaucratic systems, labor laws, visa processes, and government services remains unnecessarily difficult. Official information is often buried in Arabic-only government portals, scattered across outdated forums, or hidden behind expensive consultants.
mission.p2: URExpat exists to fix that. We believe every expatriate deserves access to clear, accurate, and up-to-date information in plain English — completely free. Our mission is to be the most trusted, comprehensive, and well-organized resource for expats living and working in Saudi Arabia.

story.label: Our Story
story.title: Why We Built This
story.p1: The founding team of URExpat are expatriates ourselves. Between us, we have collectively spent over 30 years living and working in Saudi Arabia across multiple cities. We have personally experienced the confusion of renewing an Iqama for the first time, the anxiety of understanding End of Service entitlements, and the frustration of finding contradictory information online.
story.p2: We started ExpatSaudi as the resource we wished had existed when we first arrived. Over time, it evolved into something larger: a structured, editorially rigorous platform that thousands of expats now rely on for accurate, current information about life in the Kingdom.

updates.description: Saudi regulations change frequently. We review and update our guides whenever official policies, fees, or procedures are modified by the Saudi government.

vision.label: Future Vision
vision.title: Where We Are Heading
vision.p1: ExpatSaudi is growing into a comprehensive digital platform — not just an information website. Our roadmap includes free online tools specifically designed for expats in Saudi Arabia: an Iqama expiry checker, EOSB calculator, visa fee calculator, salary calculator, and Saudi Hijri-Gregorian calendar converter.
vision.p2: We are also building a community forum where expats can share real-world experiences, ask questions, and help each other navigate life in the Kingdom. All of these features will remain completely free.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.intro: The information provided on UREXpat is intended for general informational and educational purposes only. While we aim to provide useful, accurate, and up-to-date information, users should verify important information with the relevant official authorities or qualified professionals.

sections.title: 1. General Information
paragraphs: UREXpat is an independent information platform created to help expatriates and other readers better understand life, services, procedures, and practical matters in Saudi Arabia.

The information published on this website should not be considered a substitute for official government information, legal advice, financial advice, medical advice, immigration advice, or other professional advice.

sections.title: 2. Saudi Laws, Regulations, and Government Services
paragraphs: Saudi laws, regulations, government procedures, fees, requirements, deadlines, and service availability may change without notice.
Although we make reasonable efforts to keep our content updated, UREXpat does not guarantee that every article or guide reflects the latest official requirements at the time you read it.

For important matters involving visas, residency, employment, travel, legal requirements, government services, or official procedures, users should confirm the latest information directly with the relevant Saudi government authority.

sections.title: 3. Legal and Professional Information
paragraphs: Content relating to labor law, contracts, employment rights, immigration, residency, business, taxation, or other legal matters is provided for general informational purposes only.
Nothing published on UREXpat should be interpreted as legal advice or as creating a professional-client relationship.
If you require advice regarding your specific situation, consult an appropriately qualified professional or the relevant official authority.

sections.title: 4. Financial and Banking Information
paragraphs: Financial, banking, salary, fee, currency, and cost-related information is provided for general informational purposes.
Figures, rates, fees, and calculations may change over time and may vary depending on individual circumstances, institutions, or applicable regulations.
Users should verify financial information with the relevant bank, financial institution, employer, or official authority before making financial decisions.

sections.title: 5. Healthcare Information
paragraphs: Any healthcare or medical information published on UREXpat is provided for general informational purposes only.
It should not be used as a substitute for diagnosis, treatment, or advice from a qualified healthcare professional.
For medical concerns or emergencies, contact an appropriate healthcare provider or emergency service.

sections.title: 6. Calculators and Tools
paragraphs: UREXpat may provide calculators, converters, estimators, checkers, and other interactive tools.
Results produced by these tools may be estimates and should not be considered official calculations or guarantees.
Tool results may depend on the information entered by the user and the rules or assumptions used by the calculator.
Always verify important calculations with the relevant official authority, employer, institution, or qualified professional.

sections.title: 7. Third-Party Websites and Links
paragraphs: UREXpat may link to third-party websites, including official government websites, banks, service providers, social networks, and other external resources.
These links are provided for convenience and informational purposes. UREXpat does not control or guarantee the accuracy, availability, security, or content of third-party websites.
Users should review the terms, privacy policies, and other applicable policies of external websites before using their services.

sections.title: 8. Accuracy and Updates
paragraphs: We make reasonable efforts to provide accurate and useful information, but errors, omissions, outdated information, or inaccuracies may occasionally occur.
UREXpat does not guarantee that all information is complete, accurate, current, or suitable for every individual situation.
We may update, modify, correct, or remove content at any time without prior notice.

sections.title: 9. User Responsibility

Before taking action based on important information, users should verify the relevant requirements and obtain professional advice when necessary.

sections.title: 10. No Government Affiliation

Unless explicitly stated otherwise, UREXpat is not affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by, or officially connected to any Saudi government ministry, authority, department, or government service.
